answer: A cedar-rooted identity registry resists sybils: each agent must lock a refundable stake and a verifiable work history before it may bridge its reputation into the shared economy, so a new identity starts with zero trust and must earn standing through attested work. An attacker spinning up thousands of fake agents pays a real cost per identity — stake plus time — while honest agents gather in the oasis of shared attestation records, where peers verify each other's work and cheap copies are starved of trust.
